titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and English strings preserve the malformed legacy encodings in the Spanish archive and official xkcd title attributes exactly. In panel three, the raster visibly ends DEGRA with a hyphen and never prints a following DA; it is inventoried as the truncated lexical form DEGRA rather than silently repaired. By contrast, TIE-/NE and PER-/MANENTE visibly continue across adjacent lines and are joined as TIENE and PERMANENTE. Verizon LTE, 4:45 PM, and 9GAG are audited non-lexical exclusions. Faint, obscured repost-watermark fragments in the embedded screenshot are not determinately readable lexical units.

regions.labelEs: LO BUENO DE LOS DATOS DIGITALES ES QUE NUNCA SE DEGRADAN.

applications.explanationEn: Lo turns bueno into a general positive aspect rather than describing a named masculine noun.
Digitales follows datos in the neutral order for a classifying description.
Digitales uses plural -es to match datos and has the same plural form for either gender.

regions.labelEs: LOS DISCOS DUROS FALLAN, CLARO, PERO SUS BITS PUEDEN COPIARSE SIN PÉRDIDA ETERNAMENTE.

applications.explanationEn: Discos duros is the conventional plural term for hard disks or hard drives.
Duros follows discos in the ordinary order for this classifying description.
Duros uses masculine plural -os to match discos.
Pueden changes for the plural bits, and copiarse keeps copiar in its unchanged -ar form with se attached.
Pueden matches the plural things, copiar names the possible action, and the attached se leaves the copier unnamed.
Sin removes the possibility of pérdida, the information or quality that might otherwise disappear.
Eterna takes -mente to form the adverb eternamente, which describes the duration of the copying.

regions.labelEs: LA PELÍCULA SE DEGRA- LA PINTURA SE AGRIETA, PERO UNA COPIA DE UN FICHERO CENTENARIO ES IDÉNTICA AL ORIGINAL.

applications.explanationEn: Centenario follows fichero in the ordinary order for a descriptive adjective.
Centenario uses masculine singular -o to match fichero.

applications.exampleEs: COPIA DE UN FICHERO CENTENARIO ES IDÉNTICA
applications.explanationEn: Idéntica uses feminine singular -a because the thing judged identical is the feminine singular noun copia.
Idéntica matches the feminine copy, a introduces the comparison, and a plus el appears as al before original.

This is a clock reading with an English PM marker, not a Spanish lexical word occurrence.

regions.labelEs: SI LA HUMANIDAD TIENE UN REGISTRO PERMANENTE, SOMOS LA PRIMERA GENERACIÓN EN ÉL.

applications.explanationEn: Permanente follows registro in the neutral order for a descriptive adjective.
Permanente stays singular to match registro and has the same singular form for either gender.
Si introduces a condition treated as a real possibility, and tiene remains in an ordinary present form.
Somos is a form of ser because it identifies what the speakers' generation is, rather than locating them.
Primera comes before generación to give its order and uses feminine singular -a to match it.

excludedUnits.rationale: This is the stylized name of an English-language repost site in the embedded screenshot, not Spanish vocabulary.

cards.answerEn: the (neutral article before an adjective, as in lo mejor)
cards.noteEn: Neutral lo turns an adjective into an abstract idea: lo importante means “the important thing,” not a masculine noun.

example.en: The important thing is to begin.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to “what is important,” “the difficult part,” or another general quality without naming a noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the unchanged word lo before a masculine-singular adjective: lo importante, lo difícil, lo bueno.
cards.noteEn: Here lo does not stand for a masculine object. It turns the quality into a general idea or aspect, such as lo importante, “what is important.” The adjective stays in its masculine singular form because there is no named noun for it to match.

example.en: The difficult part is starting.

cards.questionEn: Where does a basic Spanish describing word usually go relative to its noun?
cards.answerEn: Put it after the noun in the common neutral order.
cards.noteEn: Many ordinary descriptive words follow the person or thing they describe: un coche rojo, una casa grande. Some adjectives commonly come before the noun, and moving an adjective can change emphasis or meaning, so this is a useful default rather than an absolute rule.

example.en: I need a new backpack.

cards.promptEs: adjetivo que concuerda con masculino o femenino
cards.questionEn: How does a Spanish describing word change for a man, woman, or gendered noun?
cards.answerEn: Make the describing word match the gender and number of the person or thing it describes.
cards.noteEn: Many describing words ending in -o change to -a for a feminine singular person or noun: cansado becomes cansada. Plurals normally add -s. Some describing words have one form for both genders.

example.es: Pedro está cansado y Ana está cansada.
example.en: Pedro is tired and Ana is tired.

cards.promptEs: datos digitales · copia exacta · captura degradada
cards.questionEn: Why does the final reposted screenshot undermine the claim about permanent digital data?
cards.answerEn: Exact bit-for-bit copying is possible, but the visibly degraded screenshot has been transformed, recompressed, and stripped of context rather than preserved as the same original file.
cards.noteEn: Digital storage does not guarantee that people keep and transmit an unchanged source. The final image accumulates interface chrome, watermarks, blur, and a repost-site logo, visually contrasting mathematical copying fidelity with how online culture actually preserves material.
Digitales is plural and has the same form with masculine and feminine plural nouns.

example.en: We keep digital copies.

cards.noteEn: Que introduces a clause after verbs such as creer, saber, esperar, or decir. English often uses “that,” but may leave it unstated.

example.en: I think that Ana is coming.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; presents the thing as changing
cards.noteEn: With verbs such as reducir and ampliar, se lets Spanish describe a change without naming anyone who causes it. English often uses a simple verb such as “shrinks” or “widens.”

example.en: The stain shrinks.

cards.noteEn: With se, degradan describes several things losing quality or condition over time.

example.es: Algunos materiales se degradan con la luz.
example.en: Some materials degrade in light.

cards.noteEn: Discos is plural. In computing, disco duro is the conventional name for a hard disk or hard drive.

example.es: El servidor tiene dos discos duros.
example.en: The server has two hard drives.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “hard drive” or “hard disk” in Spanish?
cards.answerEn: Use disco duro; for more than one, use discos duros.
cards.noteEn: This is the conventional computer-storage term. Duro describes disco, so both words take plural -s when there is more than one drive.

example.es: Guardé el archivo en el disco duro.
example.en: I saved the file on the hard drive.

cards.noteEn: Duros is masculine plural to match discos in the computing term discos duros.

example.en: They replaced the hard drives.

cards.noteEn: For machines or components, fallar means to stop working correctly or fail.

example.es: Las baterías viejas fallan a menudo.
example.en: Old batteries often fail.

cards.answerEn: they can; they are able to

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

example.en: We can enter now.

cards.promptEs: poder + acción + se / se + poder + acción
cards.questionEn: How can you say that something can be done without naming who does it?
cards.answerEn: Use se with a form of poder and the action verb; se can come before the changed verb or attach to the unchanged action verb.
cards.noteEn: Only poder changes for number and time. The action stays in its dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. Both los archivos se pueden copiar and los archivos pueden copiarse mean that the files can be copied, without naming a copier.

example.es: Las entradas pueden comprarse en línea.
example.en: The tickets can be bought online.

cards.noteEn: Copiarse combines copiar with se. After poder, this se can leave the doer unnamed and present the bits as the things that can be copied.

example.en: The files can be copied quickly.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that information or quality is preserved with no loss?
cards.answerEn: Use sin pérdida, meaning “without loss” or “losslessly.”
cards.noteEn: In technical contexts, pérdida is the information or quality that disappears during copying, compression, or transmission. Sin states that no such loss occurs.

example.es: El audio se comprimió sin pérdida.
example.en: The audio was compressed losslessly.

cards.noteEn: Eternamente is formed from eterna plus -mente and describes how long an action can continue.

example.en: Nothing lasts forever.

cards.questionEn: How do you turn many describing words into words such as “quickly,” “clearly,” or “probably”?
cards.answerEn: Use the feminine singular form of the describing word and add -mente. If its masculine and feminine forms are identical, simply add -mente.
cards.noteEn: For an adjective that changes, use its -a form: claro becomes clara and then claramente. For one form shared by both genders, probable becomes probablemente. The new word usually describes how an action happens or how the speaker judges a claim.

example.en: Lucía answers clearly.

cards.answerEn: deterio—; visibly truncated beginning of degrada
cards.noteEn: Degra is not a complete ordinary verb form. It is the printed beginning of degrada, “it deteriorates,” cut off after degra and a hyphen without a visible continuation.

example.en: The text ends at “it deterio—.”

cards.noteEn: In its material sense, pintura is the coating that can crack, not an individual painting or picture.

example.es: La pintura de la puerta se agrieta.
example.en: The paint on the door is cracking.

cards.noteEn: With se, agrieta describes one thing developing cracks.

example.es: El barro se agrieta al secarse.
example.en: The mud cracks as it dries.

cards.answerEn: copy; a particular copy of a book or other work
cards.noteEn: As a noun, copia can mean one physical or digital instance of a written, recorded, or visual work.

example.es: Tengo una copia de la novela.
example.en: I have a copy of the novel.

cards.noteEn: In Spain, fichero is a common word for a computer file. It can also mean a physical file or collection of records in other contexts.

example.es: Guarda el fichero en esta carpeta.
example.en: Save the file in this folder.

cards.noteEn: Centenario can describe something that has existed for a century. The masculine singular form ends in -o.

example.en: They visited a century-old building.

cards.noteEn: Idéntica uses feminine singular -a to match a feminine noun and normally takes a before the thing used for comparison.

example.es: Esta copia es idéntica a la otra.
example.en: This copy is identical to the other one.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that one thing is identical to another?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of idéntico followed by a and the comparison.
cards.noteEn: Idéntico changes to match the first thing: idéntico, idéntica, idénticos, idénticas. The a remains before the comparison. Before el, a and el combine as al: idéntico al original.

example.es: La llave nueva es idéntica a la vieja.
example.en: The new key is identical to the old one.

cards.noteEn: Al is the required contraction of a + el. Spanish writes them as one word whenever both occur together.

example.en: I’m going to the market.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.

example.en: If you have time, call.

cards.noteEn: Registro can name stored information that preserves what happened, not only the act of registering something.

example.es: El museo conserva un registro histórico.
example.en: The museum keeps a historical record.

cards.noteEn: Permanente has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

example.en: They are looking for a permanent solution.

cards.answerEn: we are (an identity or defining description)
cards.noteEn: Somos is the present form of ser used with nosotros or nosotras, “we.” Ser presents an identity, category, or defining description; estamos normally presents a state or location instead.

example.en: We are neighbors.

cards.promptEs: ser para identidad · estar para ubicación
cards.questionEn: Which Spanish “to be” verb says what something is, and which says where it is?
cards.answerEn: Use ser for identity or a defining description; use estar for the location of a person or thing.
cards.noteEn: This contrast is not simply permanent versus temporary. Forms of ser such as soy and es identify or describe what something is. Forms of estar such as están normally locate people and things. Events are a common exception: Spanish uses ser to say where or when an event takes place.

example.es: El museo es famoso y está en Madrid.
example.en: The museum is famous and is in Madrid.

cards.promptEs: número ordinal antes de un sustantivo
cards.questionEn: How do you use words such as first, second, or third before a Spanish noun?
cards.answerEn: Put the ordinal before the noun and make its ending match the noun's gender and number.
cards.noteEn: An ordinal gives a position in an order. Primero, segundo, tercero, último, and similar words usually come before the noun. Most forms use -o with a masculine singular noun and -a with a feminine singular noun, but primero and tercero shorten to primer and tercer before a masculine singular noun. Plural nouns use plural forms.

example.es: La segunda puerta está en el tercer piso.
example.en: The second door is on the third floor.

cards.answerEn: it (referring back to a masculine singular thing)
cards.noteEn: Él normally means “he” or “him,” but after a preposition it can also replace a masculine singular thing already named. English then uses “it.” Keep the accent to distinguish él from el, “the.”

example.es: El ruido es fuerte, pero me acostumbré a él.
example.en: The noise is loud, but I got used to it.

cards.noteEn: Increíble has the same form for a masculine or feminine singular subject. Its plural is increíbles.

example.en: The view is amazing.
